reading.title: Marine Bioluminescence and Deep-Sea Ecosystems
reading.passage:
Bioluminescence, the production of light by living organisms, represents one of the most fascinating phenomena in marine biology. Approximately 90% of deep-sea creatures possess bioluminescent capabilities, utilizing this ability for diverse purposes including prey attraction, predator defense, and species communication. The chemical reaction between luciferin and luciferase enzymes generates photons with minimal energy waste, making it an exceptionally efficient adaptation to the perpetually dark environment below 1,000 meters.

The ecological significance of bioluminescence extends beyond individual survival. Recent research indicates that bioluminescent displays create complex visual landscapes that fundamentally structure deep-sea food webs. For instance, many zooplankton species utilize counter-illumination, producing light on their ventral surfaces to eliminate their shadows and avoid detection by predators hunting from below. This sophisticated behavior demonstrates how bioluminescence shapes predator-prey interactions in ways previously underestimated by marine biologists.

The study of bioluminescent organisms has practical applications for biotechnology and medical research. Scientists have isolated green fluorescent proteins from jellyfish, leading to revolutionary advances in cellular imaging and disease detection. Understanding how marine creatures harness light production may ultimately provide insights into sustainable energy solutions and illuminate previously unknown aspects of ocean biochemistry.

vocabulary.meaning_ko: 배쪽에 빛을 내어 자신의 그림자를 없애는 행동

questions.q: According to the passage, what is the primary advantage of bioluminescence in deep-sea organisms?
options: It provides heat energy for survival in cold temperatures
It produces light with minimal energy waste in a dark environment
It allows organisms to communicate only with their own species
It eliminates the need for other sensory organs
questions.explanation: 지문의 첫 번째 단락에서 'minimal energy waste'와 'perpetually dark environment below 1,000 meters'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 생물발광이 어두운 환경에서 효율적인 에너지 생산 방식임을 강조합니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about counter-illumination?
options: It is used exclusively by fish species
It is an aggressive hunting technique
It helps organisms avoid being detected from below
It attracts larger predators to prey organisms
questions.explanation: 두 번째 단락에서 'producing light on their ventral surfaces to eliminate their shadows and avoid detection by predators hunting from below'라고 설명되어 있습니다. 이는 아래에서 올라오는 포식자로부터 자신의 그림자를 제거하여 피하는 방법입니다.

questions.q: The word 'sophisticated' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: simple and straightforward
complex and highly developed
aggressive and dangerous
primitive and ancient
questions.explanation: 'sophisticated behavior'는 높은 수준의 복잡한 행동을 의미합니다. 역광 현상이 단순하지 않은, 진화된 적응 메커니즘임을 나타냅니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention green fluorescent proteins from jellyfish?
options: To explain how jellyfish hunt in the deep sea
To demonstrate the practical applications of studying bioluminescence
To compare jellyfish with other deep-sea creatures
To argue that jellyfish are the most important marine organisms
questions.explanation: 세 번째 단락에서 저자는 생물발광 연구의 실용적 응용을 보여주기 위해 '형광 단백질이 세포 영상화와 질병 탐지에 혁명을 가져왔다'고 언급합니다. 이는 해양 생물의 빛 생산 메커니즘 이해의 실질적 가치를 입증합니다.

sentences.original: Approximately 90% of deep-sea creatures possess bioluminescent capabilities, utilizing this ability for diverse purposes including prey attraction, predator defense, and species communication.
sentences.paraphrase: The vast majority of organisms inhabiting the deep ocean have evolved bioluminescence, employing it for multiple functions such as attracting food sources, protecting themselves from predators, and facilitating interaction with other members of their species.
sentences.tip: 명사구를 동사구로 변환하고 동의어(possess→have evolved, utilize→employ)를 사용하여 의미를 유지하면서 표현 다양화

sentences.original: The chemical reaction between luciferin and luciferase enzymes generates photons with minimal energy waste, making it an exceptionally efficient adaptation to the perpetually dark environment below 1,000 meters.
sentences.paraphrase: Because the interaction of luciferin and luciferase produces light particles while consuming very little energy, this process represents an exceptionally efficient evolutionary adaptation suited to the permanently dark conditions found in the ocean depths.
sentences.tip: 능동형 문장을 인과 관계 문장으로 재구성하고, 복합 문장을 더 간단한 구조로 분해

sentences.original: Many zooplankton species utilize counter-illumination, producing light on their ventral surfaces to eliminate their shadows and avoid detection by predators hunting from below.
sentences.paraphrase: Numerous zooplankton employ a defense mechanism whereby they generate luminescence along their undersides, thereby negating their silhouettes and escaping notice from predators approaching from beneath.
sentences.tip: 구체적 신체 부위(ventral surfaces→undersides)로 표현하고, '~하기 위해'를 '~함으로써'로 변경하여 인과 관계 재구성

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer to travel to new places and experience different cultures. Others prefer to save their money for the future and stay in their home country. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details.
model_sentences: Personally, I think traveling to new places is more valuable than saving money, because it provides unforgettable experiences and personal growth that money alone cannot buy.
First, when you travel, you encounter different cultures, traditions, and ways of thinking that broaden your perspective and make you more adaptable in life.
For example, I visited Japan last year, and staying with local families helped me understand their values and lifestyle, which changed how I view the world.
Additionally, traveling creates memories and stories that you can treasure forever, whereas money in the bank might be forgotten.
In conclusion, while saving is important, I believe that investing in travel experiences is a smarter choice for long-term happiness and personal development.

listening.title: Lecture: The Industrial Revolution and Social Change
listening.script: Professor: Today we're examining the Industrial Revolution, which fundamentally transformed society between the 1760s and 1840s. This period witnessed the shift from agrarian economies to industrial manufacturing, particularly in Britain. The steam engine, developed by James Watt, became the revolutionary technology that powered factories and transportation. Student A: Professor, did the Industrial Revolution immediately improve workers' lives? Professor: That's an insightful question. Actually, initially, factory workers endured harsh conditions—long hours, low wages, and dangerous environments. Children as young as five worked in mines and mills. However, over time, industrialization did increase overall productivity and living standards. The emergence of the middle class also created new social hierarchies. Student B: How did industrialization spread beyond Britain? Professor: Excellent point. Technology diffused to continental Europe and North America through textile machinery and engineering knowledge. Entrepreneurs and engineers migrated, bringing expertise. By the mid-1800s, industrialization had become a global phenomenon, though unequally distributed across regions.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the lecture?
options: The invention of the steam engine
The Industrial Revolution and its impact on society
Child labor laws in 19th-century Britain
The comparison between agrarian and modern economies
questions.explanation: 강의의 전체 내용은 산업혁명이 사회를 어떻게 변화시켰는지, 특히 노동 조건, 계층 구조, 그리고 세계적 확산을 다루고 있습니다.

questions.q: According to the professor, what was one of the negative effects of early industrialization?
options: It reduced the population of Britain
Workers experienced harsh conditions including low wages and long hours
It prevented the development of new technologies
The steam engine became too expensive to produce
questions.explanation: 교수는 'initially, factory workers endured harsh conditions—long hours, low wages, and dangerous environments'라고 명확히 설명했습니다. 또한 어린이들도 광산과 공장에서 일했습니다.

questions.q: Why does the professor mention the migration of entrepreneurs and engineers?
options: To explain why Britain opposed industrialization
To show how industrialization spread beyond Britain to other regions
To demonstrate that technology always moves from poor to rich countries
To argue that migration is harmful to industrial development
questions.explanation: 교수는 '기업가와 기술자들이 이주하면서 전문 지식을 가져갔고, 이를 통해 산업혁명이 대륙 유럽과 북미로 확산되었다'고 설명합니다. 이는 기술과 지식이 어떻게 국제적으로 퍼져나갔는지를 보여줍니다.
